civo_mat: Walter Mat came up the line in the rain with a photograph gone soft at the edges and nothing else. The sergeant wrote him down as Private and pointed at the mud.
One of the first hundred, Walter Mat was given the First Wave ribbon. He wrapped the accompanying paper against the damp.
Walter Mat caught a falling mug with his foot. Saving the mug was impressive; retrieving the foot without spilling it required assistance.
The transfer made Walter Mat a sapper. He spent the first hour learning where everything belonged, including himself.

The last of the jam was shared by scraping it onto a biscuit. Walter Mat approved the method. The sergeant read out the order: Verdel Ridge has fallen, hold the line. Walter Mat looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them.
The parcel for Walter Mat contained six left socks. By supper, he had found three men willing to trade.
Walter Mat saved half a biscuit for later. Later came six minutes afterwards. Mail came up the line with a letter for Walter Mat. Walter Mat read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
living_with_wild_wolves: Emil Wolves came from Stoneyford, where there is a river, a church and no mud at all. He talks about all three as if they were people.
The report confirmed the Concord victory at Verdel Ridge. Emil Wolves folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.
Emil Wolves was hit hard at Calvary Farm. Two men carried him down the communication trench on a door torn from a ruin.
Emil Wolves lay on a stretcher under a canvas sheet and watched the orderlies carry men in and out. Nobody had time to talk.
roman_askey_: Jonas "Owl" Askey unpacked a key to a house that is no longer there at R-F13. A neighbour shifted a bag to make room without asking what it was.
Jonas "Owl" Askey's First Wave ribbon drew a question at supper. He remembered the queue at the depot more clearly than the speech.

Jonas "Owl" Askey got a letter from Ilse. Two pages, one of them only about the weather back home. He read that page most. Verdel Ridge is in Concord hands. Jonas "Owl" Askey watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
The order named Jonas "Owl" Askey as Lance Corporal. He read it twice, then asked who would take over his watch.
New laces made Jonas "Owl" Askey's boots look almost respectable, until he stood up.
